messages:
sarah-sales: Heads-up — acme POC hit a flood during the demo load test and saw a bunch of 5xxs. They flagged this as a blocker for the deal. Can SE + ops triage?

devon-se: Sorry, saw this live. Which errors exactly? 503/504? Any request IDs?

sarah-sales: Stack trace from their client: 
```
2026-03-26T16:34:02Z ERROR 503 Service Unavailable - request_id=req_0a1b2c
2026-03-26T16:34:03Z ERROR 504 Gateway Timeout - request_id=req_0a1b2d
```
They said it started ~16:33 UTC and lasted ~3 minutes during a synthetic spike to 120 rps.

mira-ops: ops-bot pulled logs for those request_ids and region us-west-2. Looks like the serving pool hit capacity and requests were queued > 30s then returned 5xx. Will paste excerpt.

ops-bot: AUTOMATED: Retrieved 50 log lines for request_id=req_0a1b2c (model: redwood-v1). Summary: backend_pool_full -> enqueue -> queue_drop -> 503.

mira-ops: Relevant log snippet: 
```
[16:33:12] pool=serve-pool-3 contributors=8 queued=240
[16:33:14] enqueue request_id=req_0a1b2c tokens=110 latency_target=150ms
[16:33:44] queue_drop request_id=req_0a1b2c reason=queued_too_long
[16:33:44] response 503 request_id=req_0a1b2c
```

ashley-eng: Looks like autoscaler took ~70s to spin up extra nodes. Warmup + model load time for redwood-v1 with 8k context is ~45-90s depending on GPU. For a spike that short, burst_pool fallback should absorb it — did burst pool config exist for this customer?

devon-se: Checking their account config now. They are on trial Dedicated-style POC with burst_capacity disabled by default. They opted for strict cost controls.

sarah-sales: Customer is sensitive to costs but the demo must not fail. They asked about SLA and guaranteed demo stability. Also asked whether there's an immediate mitigation we can enable.

mira-ops: Short-term mitigation: enable burst_pool and increase queue_timeout to 60s for the POC, or temporarily route to a cheaper fallback model to avoid 5xx. We can flip a config flag on their project. I can do that now if eng approves.

ashley-eng: I can do the routing change: create a policy to fallback to redwood-v1-small (quantized) when queued > 50. Command: 
```
rwctl routing set --project acme-poc --policy "on_queue>50 -> redwood-v1-small"
```
This will reduce cost but keep success rate; will also reduce model load time.

devon-se: Also recommending: increase autoscale aggressiveness for the POC windows (scale up threshold 60% -> 40%) and enable warm spare node=1. That should cut spinup delay. I'll patch the autoscale policy.

sarah-sales: Can we do both now? Customer wants a one-click fix before the afternoon call.

mira-ops: I'll enable burst_pool and apply the routing fallback. devon, can you apply autoscale tweak?

devon-se: On it. Applying autoscale tweak now. 
```
rwctl autoscale set --project acme-poc --scale-threshold 40 --warm-spare 1
```
Patch applied.

ops-bot: CONFIG CHANGE: burst_pool=enabled for project=acme-poc by mira-ops at 2026-03-26T16:45:10Z

mira-ops: Routing fallback applied and burst_pool enabled. Recommend monitoring next 30m and share a simple test script to reproduce locally.

sarah-sales: Thanks team — I’ll tell acme we made three changes (burst, fallback, autoscale). They also asked a pricing question if they hit burst — does this incur overage charges automatically?

devon-se: Short answer: yes, burst pool uses reserved credits with a configurable burst allowance. Billing will show as "burst usage"; for POC we can cap it to a small amount and escalate if they want unlimited. I'll DM finance template for trial allowances.

ashley-eng: Follow-up action items: 1) collect more request_ids if it recurs 2) run controlled 2-minute ramp to 150 rps to validate 3) consider increasing prefix cache for repeated prompts to reduce compute.

mira-ops: I'll add a temporary alert on queue length > 100 for acme-poc and set paging to on.

sarah-sales: Perfect. I'll update the customer. If they want a deeper RCA or a security questionnaire answered (they asked about network isolation during POC), ping me and I'll route to the private deployments team. :thumbsup:

devon-se: Good plan. If any 5xxs recur, paste request_ids here and we'll escalate to runtime oncall.

sarah-sales: Closing loop — thanks everyone. Will report back after the 2pm demo. :)
